extracted.intended_audience: aircraft operators, airline maintenance/engineering organizations, certificated repair stations, and FAA/ICAO/EASA/ANAC compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for operators and maintainers to correct unsafe conditions identified in FAA airworthiness directives (ADs), including how to apply, deviate from, or substitute requirements incorporated by reference from foreign authority ADs. Covers applicability, compliance times, exceptions, methods of compliance, and documentation/IBR usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This AD applies to the specified airplane models (listed by model number) certificated in any category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must determine whether their airplane/model is listed in the AD's applicability section to know if the AD applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject identification (ATA code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each AD identifies the subject using the Air Transport Association (ATA) of America code (e.g., Code 27 Flight Controls; Code 32 Landing gear; Code 05 Time Limits/Maintenance Checks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ATA code to locate affected systems and correlate AD actions with maintenance documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsafe condition statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD must describe the unsafe condition prompting the rule (e.g., broken rod ends of aileron PCA, erroneous MLG tire width value) and the potential consequence (e.g., reduced controllability, erroneous performance calculations, runway excursions, reduced structural integrity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explanation justifies the AD and guides the urgency and nature of required actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General compliance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with this AD within the compliance times specified, unless already done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance times in the AD govern when actions must be completed; earlier-completed actions satisfy the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements via incorporation by reference (IBR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified in exceptions, comply with all required actions and compliance times specified in the referenced foreign authority AD (e.g., ANAC AD 1999-02-01R7, EASA AD 2024-0151, EASA AD 2024-0121).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must obtain and use the incorporated material (IBR) to perform the AD actions, unless the AD explicitly states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and substitutions to incorporated AD text
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the incorporated foreign AD uses certain dates, terms, paragraphs, or phrases, the FAA AD may require substituting different text or not adopting specific paragraphs (examples: replace '21 jul. 2004' with November 8, 2006; replace 'operating days' with 'days'; do not adopt certain paragraphs or the 'Remarks' section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully apply the AD's listed exceptions in place of the referenced AD's language when performing required actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial inspection/compliance times by part number
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD may specify different initial inspection compliance times depending on part number(s) of affected components (examples: P/N 394900-1003 or 394900-1005: within 3 days after Nov 8, 2006; P/N 394900-1007: within 14 days; certain 418800-series P/Ns with reinforced fittings: within 500 flight hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify component P/Ns on each airplane and apply the applicable initial compliance time for inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement/installation compliance timing (whichever occurs later)
rubrics_metrics.description: For installation/replacement actions, the AD may require accomplishing the action at the later of two specified times (examples: before accumulating 6,000 total flight hours OR within 3 days or 25 flight hours after Nov 8, 2006, whichever occurs later; or before 6,000 total flight cycles OR within 600 flight cycles after Nov 8, 2006, whichever occurs later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute both time thresholds and comply by the later one; track flight hours/cycles to determine applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection interval wording and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an incorporated AD states inspections are 'every X flight hours', the FAA AD may replace that text with 'at intervals not to exceed X flight hours' or 'at intervals not exceeding X flight hours/cycles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret required inspection intervals as maximum intervals (not necessarily fixed-period 'every') and schedule accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable methods of compliance for inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspections done before the FAA AD effective date using an AMM Task or a method approved by the Manager, International Validation Branch, FAA, or ANAC (or its delegated agent) are acceptable. Inspections on or after the effective date must use the task identified in the incorporated AD or a method approved per the FAA AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document the method used and ensure approval authority for any alternative method; maintain records showing method and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement before further flight requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an incorporated AD specifies to replace cracked and failed rod ends and PCA fittings, the FAA AD may require that all applicable replacements must be done before further flight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not return the airplane to flight until the mandated replacements are completed and recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit for previous actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD may provide credit for specified replacements or optional terminating actions if they were performed before the effective date using a specified service bulletin (example: EMBRAER Service Bulletin 145-27-0061 dated Oct 19, 1999).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain evidence (workcards, SB compliance records) showing the previous actions and conformity to the specified service bulletin to claim credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: No return of parts requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the incorporated foreign material requires sending removed parts to the parts manufacturer, the FAA AD may not include that requirement (i.e., no return-of-parts requirement in the FAA AD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators follow the FAA AD's requirements; do not send parts unless required by the FAA AD or other applicable regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Methods of Compliance (AMOCs) authority and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manager, International Validation Branch (or AIR-520 Continued Operational Safety Branch as specified), FAA, has authority to approve AMOCs for the AD if requested using procedures in 14 CFR 39.19; send requests to your principal inspector or responsible Flight Standards Office, or directly to the identified FAA manager and email AMOC@faa.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 14 CFR 39.19 when preparing AMOC requests; include supporting data; before using any approved AMOC, notify your principal inspector or the manager of the responsible Flight Standards Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting the manufacturer for instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: For any AD requirement to obtain manufacturer instructions, those instructions must be accomplished using a method approved by the FAA manager identified, or by EASA, or by the foreign authority's DOA/Designee; if approved by a foreign designee, approval must include the Designee’s authorized signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure manufacturer instructions used for compliance carry the required approval signature/authority as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required for Compliance (RC) designation and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If any material contains procedures or tests identified as RC, those procedures/tests must be done to comply with the AD; procedures/tests not identified as RC are recommended and may be deviated from using accepted methods in accordance with the operator’s maintenance/inspection program provided RCs are accomplished and the airplane is returned to an airworthy condition. Any substitutions/changes to RC procedures/tests require AMOC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat RC items as mandatory; document any deviations and obtain AMOC approval before changing RC-identified procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of maintenance/inspection program to incorporate airworthiness limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: ADs may require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program (approved AMP) to incorporate new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations or tasks specified in the incorporated EASA ADs; accomplishing the revision may terminate certain AD paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise the operator's maintenance program within the AD-specified timeframe (examples: within 90 days after the effective date or other specified period), and record the revision; the revision can serve as terminating action for some AD requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No alternative actions after program revision without approval
rubrics_metrics.description: After the maintenance/inspection program has been revised as required by the AD, no alternative actions (e.g., different inspections), intervals, or Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs) are allowed unless approved as specified in the referenced EASA AD 'Ref. Publications' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit requests for alternatives only through the approval path specified in the AD (EASA Ref. Publications approval process or AMOC).

rubrics_metrics.name: AFM revision and CPDF incorporation requirements (Airbus example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD may require revising the existing Airplane Flight Manual (AFM) to incorporate a Complementary Performance Data File (CPDF) update; to use a later AFM revision to comply, the content must be identical (not just similar) to the CPDF update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When updating AFMs, ensure the CPDF pages are incorporated exactly as specified; document AFM revision and the incorporation date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions of certain actions already required by FAA regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA AD may explicitly not require actions that are already required by existing FAA operating regulations (example: 'inform all flight crews' not required because already covered by 14 CFR sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must cross-reference existing FAA regulatory requirements to determine which incorporated AD actions are unnecessary duplicates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material availability and where to view IBR documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD lists contact points and locations where incorporated material (EASA/ANAC documents, service bulletins) can be obtained or viewed (EASA contact info and website, FAA Airworthiness Products Section address, NARA IBR locations, or regulations.gov docket).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and review incorporated documents through the listed channels before performing AD actions; maintain copies as needed for compliance records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and applicability of incorporated reference documents
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD specifies its own effective date and clarifies that references to the referenced AD's effective date must be interpreted as the FAA AD's effective date where stated; the Director of the Federal Register approves IBR materials and effective dates for incorporation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the FAA AD effective date when the AD directs substitution of dates for incorporated documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory findings and rulemaking authority statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD includes the FAA's findings under statutes and Executive Orders (examples: issuing under Subtitle VII Section 44701; certifying the AD is not a 'significant regulatory action'; no substantial effect on states or small entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statements explain the legal basis for the AD and do not alter operator compliance obligations, but are part of the rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of compliance disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD provides FAA estimates of the number of affected airplanes/operators and estimated labor and parts costs to comply (e.g., labor rate, estimated work hours, per-operator costs for program revisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cost estimates for planning; they are FAA estimates and operators should compute actual costs for scheduling and budgeting compliance work.
